findings.finding: The '# timing: hang-guard — <reason>' escape marker has no specified placement/association contract to the assert it exempts; if a single marker anywhere in a file (or loosely nearby) suppresses detection, it can silence unrelated FUTURE upper-bound asserts in the same file, undermining the detector's goal of blocking NEW unescaped asserts (AC-1).
findings.location: Plan 'Approach' section; AC-1 ('Detector blocks new unescaped upper-bound wall-clock asserts')
findings.suggested_fix: State that the marker must be on the line immediately preceding (or trailing) the specific upper-bound assert and exempts only that assert; a marker with no adjacent qualifying assert is itself a finding. Add a detector unit test: two asserts in one file, one marked → the unmarked one still fires.

findings.finding: The plan asserts '@pytest.mark.benchmark ... is unregistered' to justify why the benchmark marker is not a valid escape, but the marker IS registered (pyproject.toml:587), and --strict-markers (pyproject.toml:576) would turn any unregistered marker into a collection error — so its in-tree use proves registration. The plan's conclusion (bare benchmark marker does not remove CI flake risk) is independently verified true via the separate, load-bearing fact that no CI invocation filters `-m "not benchmark"` (the default run is `pytest -m "not integration and not external"`, _build-and-test.yml:469), so this is an inaccurate supporting rationale rather than a work-deleting false premise.
findings.location: Approach section ('the @pytest.mark.benchmark marker alone is NOT an escape; it is unregistered and no CI invocation filters -m "not benchmark"'); AC line 4
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'it is unregistered and no CI invocation filters -m "not benchmark"' with 'no CI invocation filters -m "not benchmark" (the default run is pytest -m "not integration and not external"), so the benchmark marker does not remove runner-contention flake risk — only the skipif(CI) guard does'.

findings.finding: The plan's stated rationale for treating '@pytest.mark.benchmark' as a non-escape rests on a false premise: it claims the marker 'is unregistered', but 'benchmark' IS registered in pyproject.toml (line 587: 'benchmark: performance benchmark (informational; not a pass/fail gate)'). The correct load-bearing reason is the plan's OTHER prong — the default CI suite runs 'pytest -m "not integration and not external"' (_build-and-test.yml:469), which does NOT filter benchmark tests, so the marker alone leaves runner-contention flake risk in place. The design decision is sound, but its stated justification is factually wrong, and the plan instructs the detector's teaching message + unit-test rationale to encode this reasoning.
findings.location: Approach section — NOTE on '@pytest.mark.benchmark' ... 'it is unregistered and no CI invocation filters -m "not benchmark"'
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'it is unregistered and no CI invocation filters -m "not benchmark"' with 'the default CI run (pytest -m "not integration and not external", _build-and-test.yml:469) does not exclude benchmark-marked tests, so they still execute under runner contention; only the skipif(CI) guard removes them.'
